title: Location Suitability Analyzer: Rank Places
description: Rank candidate places against weighted criteria with the Location Suitability Analyzer — a transparent score for homes, depots and trips. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, three candidate towns scored against one anchor with your weights produce a ranking you can argue with — every number in it is visible, which is the difference between analysis and vibes.
quick_answer: The Location Suitability Analyzer scores and ranks candidate places against an anchor using criteria you weight — closeness to the anchor, lower elevation, nearness to a city and more. List the candidates, set the weights, and read a transparent ranking whose arithmetic you can inspect and rerun with different priorities.

Candidate towns for a small depot, scored the same way every time — the reproducibility is the professionalism.
Elevation and city distance are built-in criteria — a stargazing base ranks by exactly what the telescope wants.
Two people, one move, different priorities: run both weight sets and see whose town survives both. Diplomacy by spreadsheet.
With closeness weighted highest, the nearest adequate town wins; slide elevation up and a smaller hill town overtakes it. The analyzer's virtue is that the flip is visible and priced in the open.
A candidate's score measures it against this list and these weights — add a fourth town and every score reshuffles honestly. The FAQs are blunt about this, on purpose.

faq: Are the scores absolute?
No — they are relative to your candidate list, anchor and weights. A score means 'best of these, by these priorities', which is the honest claim for any such tool.
What data feeds it?
Distances computed from coordinates, elevation from open elevation data, and city proximity from map data — all visible in the criteria table on this page.
Can I use the tool without sharing my precise location?
Yes — anchors and candidates are typed places; your own location is never required.
Why might a boundary or place name look different elsewhere?
Place resolution follows open geocoding data; another source may resolve a small place name to a slightly different point.
Does MapBench store my browser location?
No.
How many candidates?
A shortlist's worth — the method shines at 3 to 10. A hundred candidates deserve a spreadsheet, and this page teaches the method to copy into one.
Can I weight criteria negatively?
Weights express importance; direction (closer better, lower better) is set by the criterion's design. Combine both to express real preferences.
Is the ranking a recommendation?
It is arithmetic wearing your priorities. The visit, the lease terms and the winter test remain yours.
Same town, different anchor?
Rankings are anchor-relative by construction — a depot ranking and a family ranking of the same towns will differ, correctly.
Can I save a run?
The ranking is computed live from your inputs; note the weights beside the result in your own records and any run is reproducible exactly.
Ties between candidates?
Scores can tie — the tie is information (your criteria cannot separate them), and a visit or a new criterion breaks it honestly.
